title: Cyber Fraud & Cheating by Personation
act: Information Technology Act 2000 & Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine up to ₹1,00,000
key_elements: Use of computer resource, mobile network, or messaging application
Deceptive impersonation of bank official, enterprise, or authority
Dishonest inducement to extract OTP, credentials, or funds
procedural_guidelines: Issue immediate preservation directive under Sec 91 CrPC/BNSS to payment intermediary; register freeze order with National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (1930).
content: Cyber fraud involves fraudulent activities carried out using electronic communication, such as emails, WhatsApp, phishing links, or rogue payment interfaces. Victims are deceived into transferring money, sharing OTPs, or revealing UPI credentials. Under Section 66D of the IT Act, cheating by personation using computer resource is punishable with imprisonment up to 3 years.

title: Theft of Movable Property & Pickpocketing
act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 / Indian Penal Code
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both
key_elements: Dishonest intention to take movable property
Taking property out of possession of any person without consent
Moving of property in order to effect such taking
procedural_guidelines: Blacklist device IMEI in National CEIR portal immediately; retrieve transport junction CCTV logs within 24 hours.
content: Theft consists of dishonestly taking any movable property out of the possession of any person without their consent. In cases involving stolen mobile phones, electronic devices, or transit pickpocketing, Section 303(2) of BNS (IPC 379) applies. The offence requires demonstrating dishonest removal from victim custody.

title: Robbery & Extortion with Force or Weapon
act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 / Indian Penal Code
punishment: Rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years (14 years if committed on highway)
key_elements: Theft or extortion accomplished by causing or attempting to cause hurt
Inducing instant fear of death, grievous hurt, or wrongful restraint
Physical confrontation or weapon brandishment at the scene
procedural_guidelines: Deploy mobile forensics team to crime scene; preserve tire tracks or motorcycle surveillance footage along getaway trajectory.
content: Robbery is aggravated theft or extortion committed when the offender causes or attempts to cause death, hurt, or wrongful restraint, or fear of instant hurt. Snatching incidents involving weapons, physical assault, or threats of violence qualify as robbery under Section 309 BNS (IPC 392).

title: Criminal Breach of Trust & Fraudulent Deception
act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 / Indian Penal Code
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years and fine
key_elements: Entrustment of property or financial dominion
Dishonest misappropriation or conversion for personal enrichment
Intentional fraud, false assurances, or forged commercial documents
procedural_guidelines: Procure certified banking audit trails, agreements, and audited accounts under Sec 65B/63 Indian Evidence Act.
content: Fraud and criminal breach of trust occur when an offender is entrusted with money, assets, or property and dishonestly converts or misappropriates it for personal gain, or fraudulently induces the victim into executing a contract based on false pretexts.

title: Voluntarily Causing Hurt & Physical Assault
act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 / Indian Penal Code
punishment: Imprisonment from 1 to 3 years and fine
key_elements: Act causing bodily pain, disease, or infirmity to victim
Knowledge or intention that injury will result from the physical action
Use of force or dangerous instruments
procedural_guidelines: Refer complainant for statutory Medical Legal Examination (MLC) at Government Hospital within 6 hours.
content: Assault and voluntarily causing hurt involve acts causing bodily injury, trauma, or apprehension of immediate unlawful force. Where dangerous weapons or instruments are employed, severe statutory penalties apply under Section 117 BNS (IPC 324).

title: Cyber Stalking, Voyeurism & Electronic Harassment
section: Sec 78 BNS 2023 (Sec 354D IPC) & Sec 67 IT Act
act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 & Information Technology Act
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years (up to 5 years on repeat) and fine
key_elements: Repeated monitoring of victim internet activity, email, or social profiles
Unwanted persistent contact despite clear disinterest
Creation of defamatory impersonation handles or transmission of obscene content
procedural_guidelines: Issue notice under Sec 79(3)(b) IT Act to social media intermediary to freeze profile and disclose IP signup headers.
content: Stalking includes following, contacting, or attempting to contact a person repeatedly despite disinterest, as well as monitoring a person's internet use, social media accounts, or phone messaging. Transmission of obscene digital material additionally invokes Section 67 of the IT Act.

title: Criminal Trespass & Land Encroachment Disputes
act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 / Indian Penal Code
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 months or fine up to ₹5,000
key_elements: Entry into or upon property in possession of another
Intent to commit an offence or intimidate, insult, or annoy
Unlawfully remaining upon property after lawful entry
procedural_guidelines: Requisition municipal survey records and revenue title deeds; execute interim boundary protection report.
content: Property disputes involving unauthorized entry or boundary encroachment with intent to commit an offence or intimidate the lawful occupant constitute criminal trespass under Section 329 BNS (IPC 447). Purely civil ownership claims require reference to competent civil courts.

title: House-Breaking by Night & Criminal Burglary
act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 / Indian Penal Code
punishment: Imprisonment up to 14 years and fine
key_elements: Forced or unauthorized ingress into human dwelling
Commission of entry by night (between sunset and sunrise)
Accompanied by intent to commit theft or punishable felony
procedural_guidelines: Secure latent finger/palm prints on door hardware; summon forensic canine unit and crime scene documentation squad.
content: Burglary and house-breaking by night involve unlawful forced entry into a building or residential premises during nighttime hours with intent to commit theft. Carries severe statutory penalties under Section 331 BNS (IPC 457).

title: Identity Theft & Unauthorized Digital Access
act: Information Technology Act 2000 & Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine up to ₹1,00,000
key_elements: Fraudulent use of electronic signature, password, or biometric unique ID
Unauthorized access to email, banking, or cloud repositories
Masquerading as authentic credential holder to inflict injury or gain
procedural_guidelines: Secure server audit logs, hash values, and Multi-Factor Authentication session tokens.
content: Identity theft occurs when an offender fraudulently or dishonestly makes use of the electronic signature, password, or other unique identification feature of any other person. Section 66C of the IT Act criminalizes identity theft.

title: Admissibility & Chain of Custody of Electronic Evidence
act: Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 / Indian Evidence Act
key_elements: Verification of device source authenticity and operating integrity
Cryptographic SHA-256 hash calculation at acquisition point
Statutory certificate by person occupying responsible official position
procedural_guidelines: Generate digital hash immediately upon upload; preserve metadata and maintain unbroken forensic custody ledger.
content: Digital evidence including call logs, chat transcripts, audio recordings, and transaction screenshots requires strict compliance with electronic evidence certification standards (Section 63 BSA / 65B Indian Evidence Act). Cryptographic hashes guarantee integrity from tampering.
